amendment: 01 - separate SIP URIs and phone values
problem_statement: Native SIP currently copies the To URI user into CallAddress.To. Agent routes therefore expose agent-<assistant-id> through client.assistant_phone instead of the assistant deployment phone.
verified_context: CallAddress already contains From, To, FromURI, ToURI, and Headers.
SIP core captures complete parsed addresses in FromURI and ToURI.
The inbound pipeline maps CallAddress.From to CallerNumber and CallAddress.To to FromNumber.
The telephony streamer maps CallerNumber to client.phone and FromNumber to client.assistant_phone.
Route middleware already validates DID routes against active SIP phone deployments and loads the assistant phone deployment for agent routes.
acceptance_criteria: CallAddress retains the existing From, To, FromURI, ToURI, and Headers fields without adding replacement phone fields.
FromURI and ToURI preserve exact parsed SIP header addresses.
From and To contain phone values only and never contain SIP URIs, did- prefixes, or agent routing aliases.
Inbound DID routes set To from the validated deployment phone value.
Inbound agent routes set To from the active SIP deployment phone when configured.
Missing phone information leaves the corresponding phone field empty.
client.phone and client.assistant_phone resolve from the direction-aware phone fields.
Transfer and replacement dialogs resolve an independent four-field snapshot.
No database, protobuf, REST, SDK, UI, or non-SIP provider change is introduced.
non_goals: Use arbitrary SIP headers as trusted phone sources.
Apply E.164 conversion or country-code inference.

design.from: Caller phone extracted from the From address user when dialable.
design.to: Assistant phone resolved from the validated DID route, active SIP deployment phone, or dialable To address user.
design.metadata: Existing client.phone and client.assistant_phone mappings remain unchanged.

principles.kiss: Reuse the existing CallAddress fields and current call-context metadata path.
principles.yagni: Do not add phone fields, persistence columns, protobuf fields, UI fields, or trusted-header policy.
principles.single_ownership: SIP core owns URI capture and caller phone parsing; route middleware owns assistant phone enrichment.
principles.single_source_of_truth: The validated route and active SIP deployment determine the assistant phone.
principles.fail_safe: Unknown or non-phone values produce empty phone fields rather than aliases or fabricated numbers.
principles.observability: Record resolution source and missing-phone reason without logging raw SIP identities or phone values.
principles.least_privilege: Only tenant-scoped route and deployment data may populate the assistant phone.
principles.reversibility: Revert core extraction and route enrichment together; no stored data rollback is required.

risks: Changing client.assistant_phone from a SIP identity to a phone value changes authentication request behavior for native SIP.
An agent route may not have an active deployment phone, producing an empty assistant phone.
A permissive phone parser could misclassify SIP aliases as phone values.
Transfer code could accidentally reuse the previous dialog phone values.
Using caller-controlled SIP headers could permit authentication spoofing, so custom headers remain excluded.
required_tests: SIP core exact URI capture and phone-only From and To extraction
rollback: Revert the SIP core phone extraction and route enrichment in one change. Existing persistence and external schemas require no rollback.

open_blockers: Independent challenge and exact-digest confirmation are required before implementation.
